project.name: northstar-refunds
project.summary: LangGraph customer-support agent for Northstar that looks up orders, issues refunds through Stripe, and emails customers through SendGrid, served over a FastAPI `/chat` + `/resume` API.

acts.reason: Issues Stripe refunds and sends SendGrid emails.

consequential.reason: Refunds move money and emails reach customers.

unreviewed_consequential.reason: `issue_refund` and `send_customer_email` execute inside the agent; the approval prompt doesn't stop them.

model_decides.reason: The model chooses the order and the refund amount.

ambiguous_targets.reason: `lookup_order` finds the customer by name and takes the first match.

agents.name: support graph
agents.description: StateGraph: model → confirm → tools loop with an in-memory checkpointer; exposed by `northstar/server.py`.

consequentialActions.name: issue_refund
consequentialActions.note: Calls `stripe.Refund.create` with a model-supplied amount; retried up to 3 times.

consequentialActions.name: send_customer_email
consequentialActions.note: Sends arbitrary model-written email to any address via SendGrid; no gate at all.

consequentialActions.name: lookup_order
consequentialActions.note: Read-only, but returns customer order data chosen by fuzzy name match.

checks.finding: `Settings` defines model, keys, and URLs but no accountable owner or agent build; the `pyproject.toml` version is never read at runtime, so nothing fails when identity is absent.

evidence.note: Settings has no owner / agent name / build fields

fix.summary: Add an identity block (owner, agent name, build version) to `Settings` and refuse to start when any field is empty.
steps: Add `owner`, `agent_name`, and `build` fields to `Settings` in `northstar/config.py`, reading `build` from package metadata (`importlib.metadata.version`).
Validate them in a `Settings.__post_init__` that raises on empty values.
Test: constructing `Settings` without `NORTHSTAR_OWNER` raises a clear error.

checks.finding: A per-conversation `thread_id` exists, but there is no process instance ID, and the session reaches `issue_refund` only as a model-filled tool argument (`session_id: str = ""`), so the model decides which session a refund is logged under.

evidence.note: session_id is a tool parameter the model fills, default empty

fix.summary: Generate an instance ID at startup and inject the real thread ID into tools from the graph config instead of letting the model supply it.
steps: Create `INSTANCE_ID = uuid4()` at import time in a new `northstar/identity.py`.
Remove `session_id` from the `issue_refund` signature; read `thread_id` from the LangGraph `RunnableConfig` (`config["configurable"]["thread_id"]`) via an injected `config` parameter.
Attach `instance.id` and `session.id` to every span in `northstar/telemetry.py`.

checks.finding: Every outbound call uses one long-lived `SUPPORT_AUTOMATION_KEY`. Its comment says the returns bot and the nightly reconciler use the same key, so a call can't be traced to this agent.

evidence.note: static bearer key plus a self-declared `X-Agent-Name` header

fix.summary: Give the support agent its own workload identity and fetch short-lived tokens from the identity provider instead of a shared static key.
steps: Register a dedicated principal for the support agent (cloud managed identity or OIDC client) separate from the returns bot and reconciler.
Replace `automation_key` with a token provider (e.g. `azure.identity.DefaultAzureCredential().get_token(...)` or an OAuth client-credentials call) used by a shared HTTP client.
Delete `SUPPORT_AUTOMATION_KEY` once all three automations have their own identities.

checks.finding: Anyone can call `/chat` and `/resume`, including the endpoint that approves refunds. Outbound calls identify the agent with an `X-Agent-Name` header that any caller can forge.

evidence.note: /resume (which approves refunds) has no auth dependency

fix.summary: Require and validate a signed token (signature, issuer, audience, expiry) on `/chat` and `/resume`, and send signed tokens instead of name headers downstream.
steps: Add a FastAPI dependency in `northstar/server.py` that validates a JWT against the IdP's JWKS (`iss`, `aud`, `exp`, required claims).
Apply it to both routes; `/resume` additionally requires a reviewer role (see Permission).
Test: altered, expired, and wrong-audience tokens get 401 and never reach `agent_app.invoke`.

checks.finding: All credentials are static environment variables with no expiry, rotation, or way to disable just this agent.

fix.summary: Move to short-lived tokens from the workload identity and document a maximum lifetime and the per-agent disable procedure.
steps: Use restricted, per-agent Stripe and SendGrid keys stored in a secret manager with rotation.
Document the token lifetime and how to disable this agent's principal in `docs/identity.md`.

checks.finding: Each tool uses its own client (raw `httpx`, the Stripe SDK, the SendGrid SDK). There is no single place to attach identity or policy to outbound calls.

fix.summary: Route every external call through one governed client module and forbid raw client imports in tool code.
steps: Create `northstar/governance/clients.py` exposing `orders_client`, `refunds_client`, `email_client` that attach identity, deadlines, and policy checks.
Refactor `northstar/tools.py` to use only those clients.
Add a Ruff `banned-api` rule (or a small AST test) that fails CI if `httpx`, `stripe`, or `sendgrid` is imported outside `northstar/governance/`.

checks.finding: Tool spans carry `session.id` and `tool.name`, but the session ID is model-supplied, and there is no owner, build, instance, or action ID to tie an intent to its outcome.

fix.summary: Stamp every span and ledger record with owner, build, instance, verified session, and a per-action ID.
steps: Generate an `action_id` when a consequential tool call is proposed and pass it through approval, execution, and outcome.
Set owner/build/instance/session/action attributes in a span processor so no call site can forget them.
Make sure `Authorization` values are never logged.

checks.finding: There is no test or runbook exercising a valid-but-compromised identity, and the prerequisites (per-agent identity, revocation, permission denial) do not exist yet.

fix.summary: After per-agent identity and the stop path exist, add a staging drill that combines a valid identity with a forbidden action and then revokes it.
steps: Write `tests/drills/test_compromised_identity.py`: a valid test token attempts an unapproved refund and must be denied and recorded.
Revoke the test instance and assert subsequent calls fail within the documented deadline.

checks.finding: Graph state is a `TypedDict` and tools have typed parameters, but tool outputs are untyped dicts (`lookup_order` returns `{}` on no match) and there is no documented step map with owners or failure policy.

fix.summary: Give each tool a typed result model and document the model → confirm → tools graph with an owner and failure policy per step.
steps: Define Pydantic models `OrderLookupResult`, `RefundResult`, `EmailResult` and return them from the tools.
Add `docs/workflow.md` listing each node, its contract, owner, and what happens on failure.

checks.finding: The only tests cover the `refundable_amount` helper. Nothing tests `lookup_order`, `issue_refund`, `send_customer_email`, the `confirm_refund` node, or routing in isolation.

fix.summary: Add an isolated test module per stage with mocked neighbours.
steps: Create `tests/test_lookup_order.py`, `tests/test_issue_refund.py`, `tests/test_confirm_node.py`, and `tests/test_routing.py` with `respx`/`unittest.mock` fakes for HTTP, Stripe, and SendGrid.
Inject a known defect (e.g. wrong edge) and confirm the stage test fails.

checks.finding: `issue_refund` never calls `refundable_amount`, so the model's `amount_pence` goes straight to Stripe and the 30-day rule is never applied. The helper's tests also skip the day-30 boundary.

evidence.note: …but the refund uses the model-supplied amount

fix.summary: Compute the refund amount in code from the order and policy, cap the model's request at it, and test the boundaries.
steps: In `issue_refund`, load the order server-side and reject any `amount_pence` above `refundable_amount(order.total, order.delivered_on, today)`.
Add tests for day 30, day 31, zero, and partial amounts (Hypothesis property test: refund ≤ order total).
Block release in CI when these fail.

checks.finding: `issue_refund` retries `stripe.Refund.create` up to three times on connection errors without an idempotency key, so a timeout after Stripe accepted the first call can refund the customer twice. No failure-injection tests exist.

evidence.note: blind retry loop around a money movement

fix.summary: Pass a stable idempotency key derived from the action ID to Stripe and test timeout-after-write recovery.
steps: Call `stripe.Refund.create(..., idempotency_key=action_id)`.
Add a test that raises `APIConnectionError` after a simulated successful write and asserts exactly one refund.
Add timeout and malformed-response tests for `lookup_order`.

checks.finding: `evals/` has three cases, including the two-Alex ambiguity, but `run_evals.py` only prints a match count. Nothing fails a release.

fix.summary: Grow the dataset with consequential edge cases, add per-metric thresholds, and exit non-zero when they are missed.
steps: Add cases for day-30/31 windows, duplicate refund requests, missing receipts, wrong amounts, and tool timeouts.
Score tool choice and exact refund amount separately; `sys.exit(1)` if refund accuracy < the agreed threshold (e.g. 100% on amount).
Run it in CI against every prompt/model change.

checks.finding: The model is the floating alias `gpt-4o` and the system prompt has no version, so eval results can't be tied to what is deployed.

fix.summary: Pin a dated model version and a prompt version, and record both with the eval results in a release manifest.
steps: Pin `openai_model` to a dated snapshot and add `PROMPT_VERSION` next to `SYSTEM_PROMPT`.
Have `run_evals.py` write `release-manifest.json` with code SHA, model, prompt version, and scores.
Fail deploy when the manifest's versions don't match the running config.

checks.finding: There is no CI configuration and no test that runs the compiled graph end to end, so a broken edge (like `confirm → tools`) ships unnoticed.

fix.summary: Add a CI workflow that runs unit, contract, and end-to-end graph scenarios as a required check.
steps: Add `.github/workflows/ci.yml` running `pytest` and `python evals/run_evals.py`.
Add `tests/test_graph_e2e.py` with a fake chat model that drives refund-approved, refund-denied, and ambiguous-customer journeys.
Mark the workflow as a required status check on the main branch.

checks.finding: Spans go to a `ConsoleSpanExporter` only; there are no production metrics, sampled evaluations, alert thresholds, or owners.

fix.summary: Export traces to an observability backend, define error and refund-accuracy alerts with an owner, and connect sustained breaches to the stop path.
steps: Swap to an OTLP exporter pointed at your backend (App Insights, Honeycomb, Grafana, etc.).
Alert on tool error rate and refund-amount mismatches; route to the support-platform on-call.
Wire a sustained breach to the stop flag once Shutdown exists.

checks.finding: All three tools are registered in one flat `TOOLS` list with no risk classification; `send_customer_email` can mail any address with no policy, and a newly added tool would be callable immediately.

fix.summary: Introduce a tool registry that classifies each tool and blocks unclassified tools or destinations.
steps: Create `northstar/governance/registry.py` mapping each tool to `read | internal_write | consequential`, allowed destinations, and required reviewer role.
Build `TOOLS` from the registry and raise at startup for any tool without an entry.
Restrict `send_customer_email` recipients to the customer on the verified order.

checks.finding: Answering "no" at the approval prompt still issues the refund: the edge from `confirm` to `tools` is unconditional. `send_customer_email` has no approval step at all.

evidence.note: raw Stripe call with no approval check

fix.summary: Enforce approval inside `issue_refund` (and `send_customer_email`) so the side effect cannot run without a verified approval, and route denials away from the tool node.
steps: Add `require_approval(scope="refund")` in `northstar/governance/approval.py` and wrap the private `_issue_refund_raw`; the tool raises without a valid token.
Replace `graph.add_edge("confirm", "tools")` with a conditional edge that returns to `model` with a denial message when not approved.
Test: with approval denied, the Stripe mock is never called; calling `_issue_refund_raw` outside the wrapper fails a lint/AST check.

checks.finding: Approval is a boolean, `refund_approved`, that is never reset. After one "yes", every later refund in the conversation goes through without asking, whatever the amount.

evidence.note: skips asking once the flag is true

fix.summary: Issue a signed approval token bound to a canonical hash of `issue_refund` + `order_id` + `amount_pence` + thread + expiry, and verify it against the actual call.
steps: Compute `request_hash = sha256(canonical_json({tool, args, thread_id}))` when the call is proposed.
Have the approval service sign `{request_hash, exp, jti}`; verify signature, expiry, and hash inside `require_approval`.
Delete `refund_approved` from `State`.
Test: approve £90, then call with £900. The call must be rejected.

checks.finding: The reviewer only sees "Agent wants to issue a refund. Allow?", with no order, amount or customer. Anyone who knows the thread ID can answer it through `/resume`.

fix.summary: Show the exact refund (order, customer, amount, reason, agent version, evidence) to an authenticated reviewer role and make deny a real outcome.
steps: Pass the proposed tool call's arguments and the looked-up order into the `interrupt()` payload.
Require a `refund-reviewer` role on `/resume` and record the reviewer identity.
Test: an unauthorized user cannot approve; a deny returns to the model without calling Stripe.

checks.finding: Approval lives in an in-memory `MemorySaver` checkpointer as a flag that can be reused, never expires, and disappears on restart.

fix.summary: Store approvals in a durable store with short expiry and consume each `jti` atomically before calling Stripe.
steps: Persist approvals in Postgres/Redis with `INSERT … ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` (or `SETNX`) on `jti` at consumption time.
Reject expired tokens (minutes, not hours) and pass the action ID as Stripe's idempotency key.
Test: two concurrent calls with one token produce exactly one refund.

checks.question: Who answers the refund approval prompts in production, how many per hour do you expect, and what should happen when nobody responds?
checks.finding: The code shows a single approval prompt per thread but nothing about reviewer queues, capacity, or escalation.
The approval answer is written only to graph state; who approved, what they saw, and whether it was consumed are never recorded.

fix.summary: Record proposal, decision (verified reviewer, time), consumption, and outcome as ledger events under one action ID.
steps: Emit `refund.proposed`, `refund.approved|denied`, `approval.consumed`, and `refund.succeeded|failed|unknown` events from `require_approval` and `issue_refund`.
Store reviewer identity from the verified `/resume` token, never the bearer token itself.

checks.finding: No drill exists, and there is no stop path or ledger to exercise after a mistaken approval.

fix.summary: Once the stop path and ledger exist, add a staging drill that approves a bounded bad refund, trips the stop, and checks remediation.
steps: Write `tests/drills/test_bad_approval.py` using Stripe test mode.
Assert new work stops, credentials are revoked, and the ledger lists the refund for remediation.

checks.finding: Consequential decisions are identified by free text: `lookup_order` takes a `customer_name`, and `issue_refund` takes any `order_id`/`amount_pence` the model invents. No list of required evidence per decision exists.

fix.summary: List the refund and email decisions with their required, typed evidence (customer ID, order ID, verified amount) and define the hold path when any is missing.
steps: Add `docs/decisions.md` (or a `DECISIONS` dict in code) for `issue_refund` and `send_customer_email`.
Change tool signatures to require `customer_id` and `order_id` from a prior lookup, not names.

checks.finding: `lookup_order` silently returns `orders[0]`, so 'Refund Alex's last order' picks whichever Alex Morgan the API lists first. The only guard is the prompt line 'If you are not sure which customer is meant, ask.'

fix.summary: Add a pre-execution gate that holds any refund or email whose customer/order is not uniquely resolved and consistent across sources.
steps: Make `lookup_order` return all matches; add a `resolve_target` node between `model` and `confirm` that holds when matches ≠ 1.
Re-check that the refund's `order_id` belongs to the resolved customer before `confirm`.
Test: two Alex Morgans → the graph interrupts with a clarification, and Stripe is never called.

checks.finding: Nothing checks uniqueness, that the amount matches the order and policy, or that the conversation and order refer to the same person.

fix.summary: Hold the action when any deterministic check fails (a unique customer match, the order belongs to that customer, amount ≤ `refundable_amount`), whatever the model's confidence.
steps: Implement these checks in the `resolve_target` gate.
Return a structured hold reason naming the failed signal.

checks.finding: When no order matches, `lookup_order` returns `{}` and the model carries on; an orders-API timeout raises into the graph with no defined hold or escalation.

fix.summary: Treat missing or failed evidence as a hold with a timeout and an escalation path, never as a pass.
steps: Return an explicit `NotFound`/`Unavailable` result type from `lookup_order`.
Have the gate hold on either and escalate to a human after the timeout.

checks.finding: There is no gate to calibrate. The eval set already contains the two-Alex case, but nothing measures unsafe passes or unnecessary questions.

fix.summary: Once the gate exists, label clear and ambiguous cases and measure unsafe passes and unnecessary questions.
steps: Add 20+ labelled cases (unique vs duplicate names, mismatched orders) to `evals/refund_cases.jsonl`.
Report both rates in `run_evals.py` and fail on unsafe passes.

checks.finding: There is no clarification mechanism; whether the agent asks depends entirely on the model following the prompt, and no answer is validated.

fix.summary: Have the gate interrupt with a question naming the unresolved field and the valid options, and validate the reply against them.
steps: `interrupt({"question": "Do you mean Alex Morgan on order 4817 or on order 6234?", "options": ["4817", "6234"]})`.
Reject answers outside the options; escalate after two attempts.

checks.finding: Interrupt/resume exists via the LangGraph checkpointer and `/resume`, but `MemorySaver` loses every held action on restart, holds have no expiry, and nothing re-validates evidence before resuming.

fix.summary: Use a durable checkpointer, attach version and expiry to holds, and re-run the gate on resume.
steps: Swap `MemorySaver` for `PostgresSaver` (or `SqliteSaver` locally).
Store `expires_at` in the interrupt payload and reject late answers.
Re-run `resolve_target` after the answer, and still require Permission for the refund.

checks.finding: Holds and clarifications leave no record, so recurring ambiguity and missed errors can't be reviewed.

fix.summary: Record each hold, question, answer, and delay as ledger events and review them on a schedule.
steps: Emit `hold.created` / `hold.answered` events with the action ID.
Add a weekly review owner in `docs/operations.md`.

checks.finding: The only record is a free-form `logger.info` line and a console span; there is no versioned action-event schema.

fix.summary: Define a versioned `ActionEvent` model and emit intent, success, failure, and unknown events that validate against it.
steps: Create `northstar/governance/ledger.py` with a Pydantic `ActionEvent` (action_id, type, identities, timestamps, build/policy versions, redacted args, outcome ref).
Test that events missing `action_id` or identity are rejected.

checks.finding: Nothing is written before the refund. `issue_refund` logs only after Stripe returns, through an asynchronous exporter, so a crash mid-call leaves no record that a refund was attempted.

fix.summary: Write and await a durable intent record before calling Stripe, and refuse to call if the write fails.
steps: Call `ledger.append(intent)` (synchronous DB insert) at the top of the wrapped refund, before `stripe.Refund.create`.
Raise and skip the Stripe call if the insert isn't acknowledged.
Test: with the ledger unavailable, Stripe is never called.

checks.finding: After three failed attempts the tool raises; there is no `unknown` outcome, no idempotency key to reconcile with, and no job for stale attempts.

fix.summary: Append success/failure/unknown outcomes under the action ID and reconcile stale intents against Stripe using the idempotency key.
steps: Record `unknown` when the call errors after possibly reaching Stripe.
Add `scripts/reconcile_refunds.py` that lists intents older than N minutes without an outcome and queries Stripe by idempotency key or metadata.

checks.finding: Records go to stdout; there is no evidence store, so there is no append-only boundary or separation of read/admin rights.

fix.summary: Store action events in an append-only table or log the agent can insert into but not update or delete.
steps: Create an `action_events` table and grant the agent's DB role `INSERT` only.
Give investigators a separate read role and keep admin rights with the platform team.

checks.finding: No hash chaining or external anchoring exists.

fix.summary: Hash-link each event to the previous one and periodically anchor the chain head in a store the agent cannot write to.
steps: Add `prev_hash` and `hash` columns computed on insert.
Write the chain head hourly to an independently controlled immutable store and document the interval.

checks.finding: `log_tool_result` logs the full payload and result of any tool at INFO with no allowlist or redaction, so customer data from future tools will flow straight into logs.

fix.summary: Add a field allowlist and secret/PII scrubbing before anything reaches logs, traces, or the ledger, and set retention.
steps: Define per-tool allowlisted fields (e.g. `order_id`, `amount_pence`) and drop the rest.
Add a test that a fake card number or email address in a payload never appears in the log output.

checks.finding: No action ID exists, so there is nothing to join intent, approval, execution, and outcome on.

fix.summary: Provide a CLI that takes an action ID and prints its full linked history, flagging missing evidence.
steps: Add `scripts/investigate.py <action_id>` querying `action_events`.
Separate observed facts (receipts) from model-provided reasons in the output.

checks.finding: There are no alerts for stale intents or ledger failures, and no ledger yet to monitor.

fix.summary: Alert on overdue intents and integrity failures and hold refunds when the ledger is unhealthy; rehearse it in staging.
steps: Emit a metric for intents without outcomes older than N minutes; alert the owner.
Add `tests/drills/test_ledger_outage.py` asserting refunds are held while the ledger is down.

checks.finding: There is no way to stop the agent except killing the FastAPI process; no stop flag, admin endpoint, or control-plane action exists.

fix.summary: Add a durable stop flag with an operator-only endpoint that does not depend on the agent's cooperation.
steps: Store `stopped`, `reason`, `set_by` in Redis/Postgres via `northstar/governance/stop.py`.
Expose `POST /admin/stop` protected by an operator role (separate from reviewers).
Document how to set the flag directly if the API is down.

checks.finding: Nothing checks a stop state before model calls, tool execution, or `/resume`.

fix.summary: Check the durable stop flag in `run`, `/resume`, and inside every consequential tool wrapper.
steps: Call `stop.raise_if_stopped()` at the top of `run`, `resume`, and the `require_approval` wrapper.
Test: set the flag mid-conversation; no further tool call executes, even after a process restart.

checks.finding: `recursion_limit: 25` caps graph steps per run, but there are no limits on errors, wall-clock time, tokens/spend, or refunds per hour.

fix.summary: Add runner-enforced limits on time, errors, token spend, and refund volume that trip the stop flag with a recorded reason.
steps: Wrap `app.invoke` with a wall-clock deadline and a token budget from the model's usage metadata.
Add a per-hour refund count/amount ceiling checked in the refund wrapper.
Trip the stop flag (with reason) when any limit is breached.

checks.finding: `lookup_order` sets a 10-second timeout, but the Stripe and SendGrid calls rely on SDK defaults and there is no cancellation propagation or tracking of calls that may still complete.

fix.summary: Set explicit deadlines on every external call and record in-flight consequential calls so they reconcile to a known outcome.
steps: Configure `stripe.max_network_retries = 0` and explicit timeouts; set a timeout on the SendGrid client.
Record in-flight refunds via the ledger intent so a stop can list them.

checks.finding: Stopping the process leaves the Stripe, SendGrid and shared automation keys valid. Revoking the shared key would also stop the returns bot and the reconciler.

fix.summary: Make the stop path disable this agent's own credentials and invalidate pending approvals before any cleanup.
steps: After per-agent identities exist, have `/admin/stop` disable the agent's principal/role assignment and roll its Stripe restricted key.
Mark all unconsumed approvals as revoked in the approval store.

checks.finding: No shutdown or cleanup procedure exists.

fix.summary: Implement the stop sequence as idempotent steps with per-step deadlines: revoke, notify, then best-effort cleanup.
steps: Write `stop.execute()` running revoke → notify → flush spans → close clients, each with its own timeout.
Report unfinished steps in the stop record.

checks.finding: There is no post-stop reconciliation or owner notification, and no ledger to reconcile against.

fix.summary: On stop, list completed/failed/unknown refunds from ledger intents vs Stripe receipts and notify the agent's owner.
steps: Reuse `scripts/reconcile_refunds.py` from the stop sequence.
Send the summary to the owner configured in `Settings.owner`.

checks.finding: Nothing persists a stopped state, so a restart comes straight back up with the same keys; there is no recovery procedure or drill.

fix.summary: Keep the stop flag across restarts, require an authorized recovery with fresh credentials, and drill hard-kill and restart in staging.
steps: Check the durable stop flag at startup and refuse to serve while it is set.
Add `POST /admin/recover` requiring a separate approver.
Add `tests/drills/test_restart_stays_stopped.py`.

notes: Assessed the single agent in `northstar/`. The orders API and the approval UI are not in this repo, so their checks were judged from the agent side only.
